title: Keyboard navigation, visible focus and tab order

videos.script: Lesson 13 ended with a page that passed every automated audit. Zero violations. {{zero}} Now put the mouse away and press Tab. {{tab}} The focus lands on the name field, at the bottom of the form. Then it jumps back up to the links. You can't see any of this, because the focus ring was removed. {{jump}} Keep pressing. Show, Seat, and then the focus leaves the page. The Book button was never there. {{gone}} With a mouse, the same seat books in one click. With a keyboard, it cannot be booked at all. {{pair}} This lesson is about that difference. Which keys a tester presses, and what each one should do. {{keys}} Why a single tabindex can reorder a whole page. What a focus trap is, and a skip link. {{order}} And a script that presses Tab for you, writing down every stop, so the order becomes something you can compare. {{script}} Four small fixes later, the same script finds eight stops, in reading order, ending with a real button. {{after}}
